objective: Owner request 2026-10-02 12:45 UTC: iterate on Polymarket odds and turn them into a model, factor or strategy. Third test: does the transformed daily change of the Polymarket 2026 House and Senate Republican-control probabilities predict next-session returns of the paper's Trump-trade ETFs, banks and connected stocks (H-M, preregistered in hypotheses.md)? This is an out-of-sample check of Goldstein, Li and Wang (2026-09-03).
target_regime_and_horizon: Daily, MOC at the close of t-1 to the close of t. Backtest window: first valid signal after a 60-session burn-in (the markets exist since 2025-07-11) through 2026-10-02, about 1.4 years; forward shadow 2026-10-05 to 2026-11-04 (the session after the 2026-11-03 election). Regime: the run-up to the midterms, when odds swings are largest.
existing_solution_comparison: Published: Goldstein, Li and Wang (read in full, 2026-09-03): in 2024 a one-point rise in Polymarket's Trump probability goes with 13 bp of next-day return of Trump trades; their strategy has Sharpe 1.95 over 2024-04-01 to 11-05, in-sample, gross of costs. No replication found in the 2026-10-04 web search (the search returned unrelated 2024-election price-discovery papers). Citigroup (2026-08-17, secondary) ties midterm control odds to Treasury yields, same sign as the bond leg here. No product, open implementation or live record trades this signal. The registry has dir:prediction_market_crypto_as_equity_signal (generic lead-lag, evidence_too_weak), dir:prediction_market_macro_release_uncertainty_premium (parked) and dir:prediction_market_earnings_beat_odds (refuted 2026-10-04); none tests control-market odds against policy-sensitive assets.
remaining_evidence_gap: Whether the lead-lag exists outside the 2024 presidential election, with costs, placebos and a shift gate, on the midterm control markets. Unknown before this step: the number of daily observations of each market, whether SIP bars cover the 27 tickers (the funnel in data-feasibility.json), and how much the odds move (the House Republican price is about 8 percent, so changes may be tiny).
negative_experiments_checked: dir:prediction_market_earnings_beat_odds (refuted: odds informative but already priced by 15:00 ET; different object, company earnings contracts, not reopened); dir:prediction_market_macro_release_uncertainty_premium (parked on 79 release days; different signal); dir:prediction_market_crypto_as_equity_signal (evidence_too_weak, generic crypto odds; this test uses the paper's exact policy-odds design with a specific mechanism). Expected failures written in hypotheses.md: midterm odds move less and draw less attention, the effect was specific to 2024, the in-sample Sharpe was luck.
cost_and_execution_assumptions: Signal known at 16:00 ET on t-1, MOC entry at the close of t-1; 2 bp per side per unit position change for ETFs and large banks (and TSLA), 10 bp per side for DJT and PHUN, stress doubled; no borrow charge on the liquid shorts, stated as a caveat. Prices are public CLOB and Kalshi candlestick history, a research input only; no wallet, key or order.
stop_condition: H-M continues only if net Sharpe >= 0.5, Newey-West t >= 2.0 and the mean net return is above the 95th percentile of 1000 circular shifts (seed 20261004). Net Sharpe <= 0 refutes the midterm setting; in between is inconclusive and is decided on 2026-11-05 on backtest plus forward shadow. The forward shadow runs regardless but cannot revive a refuted line alone.

sources.claim: Goldstein, Li and Wang (2026-09-03): in Polymarket 2024-01-05..2024-11-05 a one-percentage-point rise in the Trump-win probability goes with 13 bp of next-day return of Trump trades (pooled), and a probability-based strategy shows an annualised Sharpe of 1.95 over April-November 2024; the authors state the statistics are in-sample and gross of transaction costs.
sources.applicability: The claim under out-of-sample test: same mechanism, same transformation, same assets and directions, a different election and period.
sources.limitations: Single event, in-sample, gross of costs, no independent replication found; the asset set is election-sensitive ETFs and banks, not individual stocks around announcements.
sources.independent_replication: No independent replication found in the 2026-10-04 search.

sources.claim: Goldstein, Li and Wang (2026) build the strategy signal by a 5-day EMA of the daily change in the Trump-win probability, a 60-day rolling percentile rank, and a linear map to [-1, 1]; returns are equal-weighted averages across the assets, evaluation from April 1 to the election day after a 60-session burn-in.
sources.applicability: Defines the frozen transformation of hypotheses.md.
sources.limitations: Single event, in-sample, gross of costs; the text does not state the EMA convention (adjust flag) or the rank tie rule, so the frozen design fixes pandas ewm(span=5, adjust=False) and average-rank percentiles.

sources.claim: Internet Appendix Table A.1 of the Goldstein-Li-Wang paper (included in the snapshot after the main text) gives the asset directions: all ten stock ETFs, the six banks, UUP and the three connected stocks are long a higher Trump probability, the seven Treasury ETFs are short; this matches the fallback directions frozen in hypotheses.md.
sources.applicability: Directions used verbatim; the frozen fallback was not needed.
sources.limitations: Directions come from media coverage during the 2024 cycle; the midterm control markets measure Republican Congress control, not a Trump win, so the mapping is an assumption of the out-of-sample test.

sources.claim: SECONDARY (news article, WebFetch extraction): Citigroup argues that a Democratic Congress facing a Republican president means gridlock that bond markets like, tying Polymarket midterm control odds to Treasury yields; same sign as the frozen direction of bonds short a higher Republican probability.
sources.applicability: Supports the economic sign of the bond leg only; no number enters the design.
sources.limitations: Second-hand extraction of a news article on a Citigroup note; no data or test, and the note concerns Treasury yields only, not the other asset classes.

sources.claim: Polymarket Gamma lists the events Which party will win the House in 2026 (id 32225) and Senate (id 32224), both created 2025-07-11 and ending 2026-11-04, each with separate Democratic and Republican Yes/No markets and CLOB token ids; both are unresolved on 2026-10-04.
sources.applicability: Defines the signal markets and the Republican Yes tokens.
sources.limitations: Public API without key; markets can be edited; prices are a research input only.

sources.claim: Kalshi lists CONTROLH-2026 and CONTROLS-2026 with Democratic and Republican markets open since 2024-11-06 (public candlestick endpoint, no key); used only as the robustness signal.
sources.limitations: Public market data only; no account, order or key.

sources.claim: The public CLOB /prices-history endpoint returns timestamped prices for a resolved market (daily points for fidelity 1440 in the probe); the intel notes record that hourly and finer history needs startTs/endTs windows and that interval=max with fidelity 60 returned empty.
sources.applicability: Data source for the daily 4 pm probabilities of the control markets.
sources.limitations: Probe covered one market; whether every earnings token has hourly history is the first coverage question of the build and is reported in data-feasibility.json; thin markets can have no print for days (stale flag).

sources.claim: Kalshi distributions are accurate forecasts of macro outcomes (for headline CPI a statistically significant improvement over the Bloomberg consensus); the paper tests forecast accuracy and news response, not stock returns.
sources.applicability: Shows regulated event-contract prices carry real information; motivates the Kalshi robustness signal, no stock-return test.
sources.limitations: Macro releases on Kalshi, not company earnings on Polymarket; accuracy is not the same as tradable alpha after the stock market already prices the information.
sources.independent_replication: Replication code by a third party (WillBtK/macro_kalshi) rebuilds the distributions; no independent replication of the forecast claims found.

sources.claim: Qin and Yang (arXiv 2606.04217) describe the Polymarket-v1 on-chain trade archive, 2022-11-21 to 2026-04-28, 1.20 billion trades, and show that tick-rule and bulk-volume classifiers are near random on it.
sources.applicability: Last prints in thin Polymarket markets are noisy; the daily 16:00 ET price is taken from the last CLOB point and a missing session carries the last price.
sources.limitations: A data and microstructure paper with no stock-return test.

sources.claim: Leigh, Wolfers and Zitzewitz (NBER w9587, 2003): the price of a prediction-market security on Saddam Hussein's survival moves with spot oil and equity-sector prices, so an event probability can be mapped to asset returns by a stated policy channel; 20-year-old precedent for translating event odds into asset exposures.
sources.applicability: Precedent for the mapping of event odds to policy-sensitive assets; no number enters the design.
sources.limitations: Different event, a 2003 high-frequency study of one security, no trading strategy or costs; the intel snapshot was read from the NBER PDF text.

cheapest_decisive_test.action: After the candidate manifest is committed and pre-backtest validation passes: scripts/run_h20261004_pm_midterm_odds_leadlag.py joins the control-market probabilities to SIP daily closes and runs H-M, the three continue-rule gates, the predictive regression, categories, the Kalshi variant and the placebos in one pass.
cheapest_decisive_test.pass_condition: Net Sharpe >= 0.5, NW t >= 2.0 and mean net return above the 95th percentile of the 1000 circular shifts.
cheapest_decisive_test.falsification_condition: Net Sharpe <= 0: H-M refuted for the midterm setting; the registry row dir:prediction_market_policy_odds_leadlag_glw2026 is recorded as refuted with the numbers and the power statement.
